decisions.Acceptance criteria: No row or value is altered by equality-only deduplication or a generic IQR rule.
decisions.Operation: Do not drop exact row matches without independent source identity evidence; do not delete, clip, winsorize, or replace values solely because they are IQR outlier candidates.
decisions.Rationale: The source provides no observation identifier, while numerical extremes remain domain-valid measurements.
decisions.Title: Prohibit unsupported deduplication and generic outlier treatment

decisions.Acceptance criteria: Prepared row count and values match the validated source before any split or learned transformation.
decisions.Operation: Create a defensive prepared copy without changing values, row count, column semantics, or target labels.
decisions.Rationale: Source-backed type, domain, and value checks found no deterministic repair requirement.
decisions.Title: Preserve the validated source observations

decisions.Acceptance criteria: Prepared y contains exactly the declared class set and X never contains the target.
decisions.Operation: Keep every declared class label readable in prepared data and exclude the target and any target derivative from predictors.
decisions.Rationale: All declared classes are observed and no binary positive-class semantics apply.
decisions.Title: Preserve the nominal multiclass target contract

decisions.Acceptance criteria: Baseline X contains exactly the declared candidate features.
decisions.Operation: Start downstream model evaluation with all validated numerical candidate features, including documented derived measurements.
decisions.Rationale: Correlation and mathematical redundancy are exploratory evidence, not sufficient grounds for global feature deletion.
decisions.Title: Use the complete validated candidate-feature set as the baseline

decisions.Acceptance criteria: Partitions are reproducible, disjoint, preserve every target class, and keep the final test holdout untouched.
decisions.Operation: Partition the validated snapshot into 70% train, 15% validation, and 15% test with stratification by Class and random seed 42.
decisions.Rationale: The released table has no chronological evaluation field, while unequal multiclass support makes stratification important.
decisions.Title: Use a reproducible stratified snapshot split

decisions.Acceptance criteria: All learned operations record train-only fit scope and the final test partition is used only after the model contract is frozen.
decisions.Operation: Perform the approved split before fitting scalers, selectors, resampling strategies, target-aware rankings, or model parameters.
decisions.Rationale: Held-out partitions must not influence learned preparation choices.
decisions.Title: Split before every learned target-aware or distribution-aware operation

decisions.Acceptance criteria: Any scaler is fitted on training data only; validation and test are transform-only and never refit preprocessing.
decisions.Operation: Preserve original numerical values and fit scaling only inside candidate pipelines whose model family requires or benefits from it.
decisions.Rationale: All predictors are numerical, but scale sensitivity depends on model family.
decisions.Title: Make numerical scaling model-dependent and train-fitted

decisions.Acceptance criteria: Any imbalance strategy is evaluated inside training/validation; validation and test prevalence remains untouched.
decisions.Operation: Use stratification as the baseline policy and compare class weighting or training-only resampling only if validation evidence shows a benefit for macro and per-class metrics.
decisions.Rationale: Class support is unequal, but frequency alone does not justify altering the released distribution.
decisions.Title: Defer class-imbalance mitigation to model selection

decisions.Acceptance criteria: No feature is removed globally from EDA rankings; any reduced set must match or improve validation objectives before adoption.
decisions.Operation: Compare the all-feature baseline with regularized or ablated feature sets using training and validation evidence only.
decisions.Rationale: 21 feature pair(s) meet the declared redundancy review rule and multiple measurements are mathematically derived.
decisions.Title: Defer redundancy reduction to leakage-safe ablation

decisions.Acceptance criteria: Each unresolved dependency is either source-verified or treated as an ordinary candidate feature during model evaluation.
decisions.Operation: Retain these features in the baseline and verify source formula or tolerance assumptions before using dependency claims to prune them.
decisions.Rationale: At least one declared mathematical dependency did not reproduce the released values within the exploratory tolerance.
decisions.Title: Keep unconfirmed derived dependencies out of automatic pruning

execution_plan.Acceptance criteria: Validation and test are transform-only and no scaler is globally fitted.
execution_plan.Action: Fit model-dependent numerical preprocessing on training data only.

execution_plan.Acceptance criteria: Alternatives are adopted only from training/validation evidence.
execution_plan.Action: Evaluate imbalance and redundancy alternatives without changing the baseline handoff.

guardrails.Prohibited operation: Modify or overwrite the acquired raw table in place.
guardrails.Rationale: Reproducible preparation requires immutable source evidence.
guardrails.Title: Preserve the raw evidence
guardrails.Verification: Raw shape, values, index, and dtypes remain unchanged.

guardrails.Prohibited operation: Include the target or a direct derivative in X or feature transformations.
guardrails.Rationale: This would constitute direct target leakage.
guardrails.Title: Keep the target outside predictors
guardrails.Verification: Predictor matrices contain exactly candidate features and never the target.

guardrails.Prohibited operation: Fit scaling, selection, resampling, or learned transformations before splitting or on held-out data.
guardrails.Rationale: Held-out data must not influence learned preparation parameters.
guardrails.Title: Fit learned preprocessing on training only
guardrails.Verification: Every learned transformer records train-only fit scope.

guardrails.Prohibited operation: Over- or undersample validation or test partitions.
guardrails.Rationale: Held-out prevalence must remain representative of the released snapshot.
guardrails.Title: Do not resample validation or test
guardrails.Verification: Validation and test row sets retain their original class composition.

guardrails.Prohibited operation: Use full-data target associations or redundancy rankings to choose the final feature set.
guardrails.Rationale: Global selection would bias held-out evaluation.
guardrails.Title: Do not select features globally
guardrails.Verification: Ablation and selection use training/validation evidence only.

guardrails.Prohibited operation: Use final-test metrics for model, feature, resampling, or hyperparameter selection.
guardrails.Rationale: Repeated test access converts the final holdout into validation data.
guardrails.Title: Protect the final test holdout
guardrails.Verification: Final test evaluation occurs only after the analysis contract is frozen.

guardrails.Prohibited operation: Drop exact matches without independent observation identity evidence.
guardrails.Rationale: The released Dry Bean table does not provide a source observation identifier.
guardrails.Title: Do not deduplicate from row equality alone
guardrails.Verification: No source row is removed solely because all released values match another row.

guardrails.Prohibited operation: Delete, clip, winsorize, or replace values solely from an IQR flag.
guardrails.Rationale: IQR flags are distributional evidence and the audited values remain domain-valid.
guardrails.Title: Do not apply generic outlier cleaning
guardrails.Verification: The baseline prepared projection preserves every numerical value.
